headline: South Asia: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
- Africa: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
- Western Russia: Drone Strikes Kill 2 in Kursk and Bryansk Regions Amid Overnight Attacks.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: RELIEF LAWSUIT - Pastor challenges NIDS requirement for hurricane aid.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 14 hours ago: RELIEF LAWSUIT - Pastor challenges NIDS requirement for hurricane aid.
Pastor Jeffrey Shuttleworth has filed a judicial review application in the Supreme Court challenging the Government’s decision requiring Jamaicans to register under the National Identification System (NIDS) to access Hurricane Melissa relief assistance. The senior pastor of Freedom Come Ministries International wants the Supreme Court to declare the decision illegal, null and void, and quash the requirement through an order of certiorari, as well as award costs.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 14 hours ago: Constitutional red flag raised over power to sell property for unpaid fees.
Solicitor General Marlene Aldred on Thursday raised a red flag in relation to Section 35(1) of the Registration (Shared Community) Act 2026, arguing that it is not consistent with Section 15 of the Constitution. Her pronouncement followed committee member Cleveland Tomlinson’s identification of an inconsistency in the bill, which he said warranted careful review.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Drone Strikes Kill 2 in Kursk and Bryansk Regions Amid Overnight Attacks.
- The Moscow Times, 8 hours ago: Drone Strikes Kill 2 in Kursk and Bryansk Regions Amid Overnight Attacks.
In St. Petersburg, falling drone debris reportedly wounded a 44-year-old woman after damaging an apartment building.
- Ukrainska Pravda, South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, Africanews, 6 hours ago: "They were trying to build their lives": IT couple killed in Russian drone attack on Kharkiv.
A Russian Shahed drone hit a 15th-floor flat in Kharkiv on 26 November, killing 38-year-old IT specialists Daria and Valerii along with their cat.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russians attack civilian business in Zhytomyr Oblast: one killed, 12 injured.
One person was killed and 12 were injured in a Russian strike on a civilian business in Zhytomyr Oblast's Malyn hromada on the afternoon of 27 November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian forces attack Lozova with jet-powered drones, injuring two people.
Russian forces struck Lozova in Kharkiv Oblast with jet-powered drones on 27 November, injuring two people and sparking fires at a house and warehouse.
Southern Europe - bottom line: We’d be ‘stupid’ not to: Poland defends $300M military AI deal with Palantir.
- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: We’d be ‘stupid’ not to: Poland defends $300M military AI deal with Palantir.
Poland's defense minister said it would be “wrong” not to use the software, despite concerns over reliance on American technology.
- Politico Europe, 11 hours ago: ‘Islam is Sharia’: Germany’s far-right leader attacks Le Pen on Muslims and Europe.
AfD’s Alice Weidel talks mass deportations, the right to Israel’s existence and peace with Russia.
- Balkan Insight, 12 hours ago: Democracy Digest: V4 Remain Critical of Budget as EU Summit Ends Without Deal.
Elsewhere, Ukrainian youth in hospital after setting himself on fire opposite Warsaw’s presidential palace; postal voting scrapped for Slovakia’s 2027 election; EU Parliament warns against Czechia’s public media reforms.
- Politico Europe, 17 hours ago: Bank of England boss warns AI must benefit humans.
Tech needs boundaries — "a bit like rearing children," says Andrew Bailey.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
- Africanews, 11 hours ago: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
Algeria on Thursday condemned what it called the ‘spillover’ of the war in Ukraine into Libya, after Kyiv’s attack on two Russian vessels off eastern Libya. Two Libyan soldiers were killed in Sunday’s drone strikes which sank a Russian warship and targeted a cargo ship in Libyan waters.
- Africanews, 11 hours ago: Italy says not informed about Ukraine drone strike on Russian ships in Libya.
Italy has joined the voices expressing concern about Ukraine’s attack on Russia ships in Libyan waters. Rome was not informed of Sunday’s drone strike, the country’s foreign minister told parliament on Thursday, warning that further military action could jeopardise efforts to reunify Libya.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 15 hours ago: Sudan: UN Condemns Drone Strikes That Killed 17 Civilians in Blue Nile.
[Dabanga] The United Nations has condemned drone strikes in Blue Nile that reportedly killed 17 civilians in Ed Damazin, as fighting escalates, and displacement deepens across the region. UN Secretary-General spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday that the UN remained "deeply concerned by the escalation of hostilities in Blue Nile state", which had reportedly caused civilian deaths and injuries.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Nigeria: 3 Killed in Attack On Hausa Quarters in Delta.
[Daily Trust] Three persons have been killed following an attack by suspected hoodlums on the Hausa quarters in Warri, Warri South Local Government Area of Delta State.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: US military strikes cargo ship from Bandar Abbas in Gulf of Oman, says it tried to breach blockade.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: US military strikes cargo ship from Bandar Abbas in Gulf of Oman, says it tried to breach blockade.
CENTCOM said the Palau-flagged Pacific Archer had left Iran’s Bandar Abbas port and ignored repeated warnings. The strike disabled the ship’s propulsion, but no crew members were injured.
- Jerusalem Post, The Moscow Times, just now: Russian military flotilla heading to Libya turned around after Ukrainian drones sunk warship.
A Ukrainian military intelligence official familiar with the convoy confirmed that a second flotilla had turned from heading to Libya and was now paused off the coast of Algeria.
- Jerusalem Post, 7 hours ago: Hamas confirms son of Khalil al-Hayya targeted in Gaza, claims no casualties following strike.
According to the report, the son's fate remains unknown, and six Palestinians were wounded in the strike, with injuries of varying degrees.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Trump backs Iraqi PM’s oil smuggling crackdown.
Baghdad closes border crossings as Kurdish authorities warn of constitutional violations and call for meeting.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Malawian Killed Fighting for Russia in Ukraine War.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 13 hours ago: Malawi: Malawian Killed Fighting for Russia in Ukraine War.
[Nyasa Times] The family of a Malawian driver who vanished from Blantyre has been left reeling after learning he was killed while fighting for Russia against Ukraine.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Police to Name and Shame Companies Selling Counterfeit Agricultural Inputs.
[New Zimbabwe] THE Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) has warned that it will name and shame backyard garages, unregistered companies and individuals involved in manufacturing and selling counterfeit agricultural inputs to farmers.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: South Africa: South Africa's Border Management Plans Drone Surveillance and Tighter Security for 2026/27 Festive Season.
[New Zimbabwe] The South African Border Management Authority (BMA) is preparing to intensify border security during the 2026/2027 festive season, including deploying drones at vulnerable crossing points to curb illegal activity.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement’s top decision-making body on Friday reviewed the regional security situation and condemned “persistent and heinous” Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. A meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) was held in the federal capital, where authorities announced a public holiday and imposed special movement restrictions in view of the high-level gathering. A local holiday was also announced in Rawalpindi. The SPDC comprises the foreign and defence ministers and top military officials of the three countries.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Pakistan Shaheens cruise into Asia Cup Rising Stars final with five-wicket win over Bangladesh ‘A’.
Pakistan Shaheens produced a composed five-wicket victory over Bangladesh ‘A’ in the second semi-final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars on Friday, chasing down a target of 233 with 28 balls to spare to book their place in Sunday’s final against Sri Lanka ‘A’. The defending champions reached 233-5 in 45.2 overs after Bangladesh ‘A’ had posted 232-8 in their 50 overs. Hasan Nawaz, who made 62 and claimed two wickets, was named player of the match.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: Erdogan completes Turkiye's ratification of Makkah defence pact.
President Tayyip Erdogan has formally approved the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the country’s Official Gazette said on Friday, completing Turkiye’s ratification after parliament ratified it earlier this month. Turkiye’s parliament ratified the agreement on November 5, paving the way for Ankara to support Riyadh amid attacks by Yemen’s Houthi militia against the kingdom. Under the agreement, an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all.
- The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: Saudi strike kills 11 in Yemen, reports Houthi media.
The latest incidents came a day after a deadly Houthi attack on a Saudi oil refinery, and add to a growing tally of violence since Yemen's civil war reignited over the summer
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: North Korean defector apprehended while moving toward inter-Korean border fence.
- NK News, 13 hours ago: North Korean defector apprehended while moving toward inter-Korean border fence.
A North Korean defector moving north toward the inter-Korean border fence in Cheorwon County was apprehended by South Korean troops Thursday evening, according to Seoul’s defense authorities. South Korean troops caught the woman in her 30s in an area north of the Civilian Control Line (CCL), a boundary that runs several kilometers south of the […]
- Yonhap News Agency, 19 hours ago: 2 S. Korean naval submarines under repair after accidents.
SEOUL, Nov. 27 (Yonhap) -- Two of the South Korean Navy's attack submarines are ...
Asia - bottom line: China-Cambodia drills: Type 071 warship offloads tanks overseas for the first time.
- South China Morning Post - China, 12 hours ago: China-Cambodia drills: Type 071 warship offloads tanks overseas for the first time.
China has for the first time sent its main battle tanks via an amphibious transport dock to Southeast Asia for a 15-day joint military exercise with Cambodia. The drills began on Wednesday at the Cambodia-China Joint Support and Training Centre, which opened early last year at Ream Port – a strategically located Cambodian naval base. The facility is expected to play a role as Beijing seeks to bypass maritime chokepoints and improve access to the Andaman Sea. Type 96A main battle tanks – one of...
- Taipei Times, just now: Taiwan rules out office name change amid Lithuanian warning.
- Taipei Times, just now: 2026 Elections:  Group urges cybersecurity awareness ahead of vote.
- Taipei Times, just now: An eBay find brings postwar Taiwan into focus.
India - bottom line: Man sexually assaults 60-year-old woman inside Mumbai railway station washroom, arrested.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Man sexually assaults 60-year-old woman inside Mumbai railway station washroom, arrested.
In a shocking incident at Ghatkopar railway station, a 60-year-old woman was attacked in a washroom late Thursday night while with her daughter. The suspect, recorded by CCTV, entered the facility shortly before midnight. After reporting the assault, the woman helped authorities quickly track down the attacker, leading to the arrest of a 25-year-old man, Taslim Noor Mohammad.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: Drone hits 'Dhurandhar' rapper Reble in face during performance at Guwahati award event.
Rapper Reble was performing at the PULSE 2026 Awards when a drone struck her in the face. After being hit, she abruptly left the stage without addressing the audience or providing further information. Footage of the incident has circulated on social media, sparking concerns among fans and criticism of the event's organizers. Many users expressed worries for Reble's safety and called for better event management.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: OpenAI Accuses Apple Of Stealing Trade Secrets In New Lawsuit: Report.
OpenAI has launched a new legal action against Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, the Financial Times reported on Friday.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Husband took late wife's $623k asbestos payout; 3 children awarded over $301k.
Lionel Adams Sr. from Louisiana faced a setback as the court denied his appeal concerning his late wife Ora Jean Adams' asbestos settlement funds. The verdict revealed that the funds, which were not legally gifted to him prior to her passing, remained with their three children. The court ruled that he must pay them over $301,000, honoring their mother's intent to distribute the money equally.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: ABC 50/50 quiz: Duran Duran, Countdown vs Hey Hey, and is this a spider or a moth?.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: ABC 50/50 quiz: Duran Duran, Countdown vs Hey Hey, and is this a spider or a moth?.
Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, the other is wrong. But be warned: we might try to trick you.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Comedian Adam Kay on hospital nightshifts and six things he won't throw away.
Adam Kay says it's rare for people to thank their doctors, and some of his most prized possessions are cards from former patients. He has turned his time working the wards into a new comedy show.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: What are Taiwan's 'nine-in-one' elections and why should we care?.
Analysts say the elections will be watched closely by Beijing, while Taiwan has warned against possible Chinese interference.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
